newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - flat, next week seen same.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - flat, next week seen same.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices headed into Friday's early close unchanged in extremely quiet trading, as market participants said they see little next week likely to spark activity.
"It's been very quiet and I don't expect much different than that next week until we see some cash flows into the mutual funds," one muni trader said.
Scheduled competitive and negotiated municipal bond sales for the week of Jan 20 are expected to total just $1.8 billion in 81 offerings, according to Reuters Municipal Bond Information Group.

Competitive sales total $409 million million in 44 sales, while negotiated sales total $1.4 billion in 37 offerings. The largest negotiated deal is a $150 million Platte River Power Authority, Colo, issue through Smith Barney Inc.
The Treasury market is also relatively quiet heading into the early close Friday, with the long bond up 3/32 at 95-28/32 to yield 6.82 percent.
Debt futures were higher. The March municipal contract was up 6/32 at 114-18/32 and March T-bonds rose 9/32 to 111. The MOB spread was 114 ticks, narrowing from 117 at the close Thursday.
In the muni secondary, bids on Houston water and sewer FGIC 5-1/4s of 2022 were unchanged at 5.76 percent net.
